Skills

Create /slash commands that give Claude domain knowledge and automate repeatable workflows.

What Are Skills?

A skill is a directory with a SKILL.md file. Create one and Claude adds it to its toolkit — either invoked with /skill-name or loaded automatically when relevant to your conversation.

~/.claude/skills/
All your projects
e.g. personal coding conventions
.claude/skills/
This project only
e.g. project-specific deploy script
plugin skills
When plugin is enabled
e.g. shared team skills

Built-in Bundled Skills

These ship with every Claude Code installation:

/simplify

Reviews your recently changed files for code reuse, quality, and efficiency. Spawns 3 parallel review agents.

/batch <instruction>

Large-scale parallel changes across a codebase. Decomposes into 5–30 independent tasks, each in its own worktree with its own PR.

/debug [description]

Troubleshoots your current Claude Code session by reading the debug log.

/claude-api

Loads Claude API reference for your language. Also activates automatically when you import the anthropic SDK.

Create Your First Skill

bash
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">mkdir -p ~/."color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude/skills/explain-code
~/.claude/skills/explain-code/SKILL.mdmarkdown
---
name: explain-code
description: Explains code with visual diagrams and analogies. Use when
  explaining how code works, teaching about a codebase, or when the user
  asks "how does this work?"
---

When explaining code, always include:

1. **Start with an analogy**: Compare the code to something from everyday life
2. **Draw a diagram**: Use ASCII art to show the flow or relationships
3. **Walk through the code**: Explain step-by-step what happens
4. **Highlight a gotcha**: What's a common mistake or misconception?

Keep explanations conversational. For complex concepts, use multiple analogies.

Test it two ways:

bash
"color:#586e75"># Let Claude invoke it automatically:
How does this code work?

"color:#586e75"># Or invoke directly:
/explain-code src/auth/login.ts

Frontmatter Reference

SKILL.md frontmatteryaml
---
#818cf8">name: my-skill                    # Becomes /my-skill command
#818cf8">description: What it does         # Claude uses this to decide when to load it
#818cf8">argument-hint: [issue-number]     # Shown in autocomplete
#818cf8">disable-model-invocation: true    # Only YOU can invoke (not Claude auto)
#818cf8">user-invocable: false             # Only Claude invokes (hidden from / menu)
#818cf8">allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob   # Tools allowed without asking permission
#818cf8">model: opus                       # Specific model for this skill
#818cf8">context: fork                     # Run in isolated subagent context
#818cf8">agent: Explore                    # Which subagent type to use
---

Pass Arguments

.claude/skills/fix-issue/SKILL.mdmarkdown
---
name: fix-issue
description: Fix a GitHub issue by number
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Fix GitHub issue $ARGUMENTS following our coding standards.

1. Read the issue with `gh issue view $ARGUMENTS`
2. Understand the requirements
3. Implement the fix
4. Write tests
5. Create a commit and PR
bash
/fix-issue 123
"color:#586e75"># → Claude receives "Fix GitHub issue 123 following our coding standards..."

Access specific arguments by position with $ARGUMENTS[0], $0, etc:

markdown
---
name: migrate-component
---

Migrate the $0 component from $1 to $2.
Preserve all existing behavior and tests.
bash
/migrate-component SearchBar React Vue

Dynamic Context Injection

Use !`command` syntax to run shell commands before the skill runs. The output is injected into the prompt — Claude sees real data, not the command:

pr-summary SKILL.mdmarkdown
---
name: pr-summary
description: Summarize changes in a pull request
context: fork
agent: Explore
allowed-tools: Bash(gh *)
---

## Pull request context
- PR diff: !`gh pr diff`
- PR comments: !`gh pr view --comments`
- Changed files: !`gh pr diff --name-only`

## Your task
Summarize this PR for the team — key changes, risks, and testing notes.
